claims.claim: Jeremy Howard of Answer.AI proposed the /llms.txt file in a post dated September 3, 2024, suggesting sites add it to provide LLM-friendly content.
claims.reason: Byline Jeremy Howard, Sept 3, 2024: "We propose that those interested in providing LLM-friendly content add a /llms.txt file to their site."

claims.claim: The llms.txt spec, now published as v2 at llmstxt.org, places the file at the root path /llms.txt, or at a subpath such as /docs/llms.txt that covers the URLs under it.
claims.reason: Titled "The /llms.txt file, v2"; applies to files "at the root path /llms.txt ... or at any subpath (e.g. /docs/llms.txt)."

claims.claim: An H1 with the site or project name is the only required section; it is followed by a blockquote summary, optional detail, and H2 sections holding markdown lists of links.
claims.reason: Spec: H1 is the only required section, then a blockquote summary, optional detail paragraphs, and H2-delimited file lists of markdown links.

claims.claim: By convention, an H2 section titled "Optional" holds secondary information: links an agent can skip when a shorter context is needed.
claims.reason: "The 'Optional' section is used, by convention, for secondary information: links an agent can skip when a shorter context is needed."

claims.claim: The proposal says robots.txt tells automated tools what access is acceptable, while llms.txt is used on demand, when an agent needs information while assisting a user.
claims.reason: "robots.txt lets automated tools know what access ... is considered acceptable"; llms.txt "is instead used on demand, when an agent needs information ..."

claims.claim: The proposal says sitemap.xml is no substitute: it often lacks LLM-readable page versions and covers more content than fits in an LLM context window.
claims.reason: sitemap.xml "Often won't have the LLM-readable versions of pages listed" and covers documents "too large to fit in an LLM context window."

claims.claim: robots.txt is standardized as the Robots Exclusion Protocol in RFC 9309 (September 2022), which states its rules "are not a form of access authorization."
claims.reason: RFC 9309 dated September 2022; text: "These rules are not a form of access authorization."

claims.claim: A sitemap is an XML file listing a site's URLs with metadata for each: when it was last updated, how often it changes, and its relative importance.
claims.reason: XML file listing URLs with metadata: "when it was last updated, how often it usually changes, and how important it is, relative to other URLs in the site."

claims.claim: Mintlify says it shipped llms.txt support across every site on its platform in 2024, and that it and Anthropic then developed llms-full.txt together.
claims.reason: "When Mintlify shipped llms.txt support across every site on the platform in 2024..."; "The two teams then developed llms-full.txt together."

claims.claim: Google's AI optimization guide (updated July 10, 2026) says you don't need AI text files or Markdown to appear in Google Search, and that Google Search ignores llms.txt files.
claims.sourceName: Google Search Central: AI optimization guide
claims.reason: Updated July 10, 2026: no need for "AI text files, markup, or Markdown"; fine to create LLMS.txt files for other services, but "Google Search ignores them."

claims.claim: In April 2025 Google's John Mueller wrote on Reddit that no AI services had said they use llms.txt, comparing it to the keywords meta tag.
claims.reason: SEJ, Apr 17, 2025, quotes Mueller on Reddit: "AFAIK none of the AI services have said they're using LLMs.TXT ... comparable to the keywords meta tag."

claims.claim: Chrome's Lighthouse llms.txt audit flags a page if a server error occurs fetching llms.txt; a 404 marks it Not Applicable, since the file is optional. Doc last updated 2026-05-05.
claims.sourceName: Chrome for Developers: Lighthouse llms.txt audit
claims.reason: "Lighthouse flags the pages if a server error occurs"; a 404 is "marked as Not Applicable (N/A), as providing the file is optional." Updated 2026-05-05.

claims.claim: OpenAI says GPTBot crawls content that may train its foundation models, OAI-SearchBot surfaces sites in ChatGPT search, and ChatGPT-User visits pages for user actions.
claims.reason: GPTBot crawls "content that may be used in training"; OAI-SearchBot "surface[s] websites in search results in ChatGPT"; ChatGPT-User for "certain user actions."

claims.claim: OpenAI publishes IP ranges for its three bots at openai.com/gptbot.json, openai.com/searchbot.json and openai.com/chatgpt-user.json.
claims.reason: Page lists IP range files openai.com/gptbot.json, openai.com/searchbot.json and openai.com/chatgpt-user.json.

claims.claim: OpenAI's crawler documentation page links to OpenAI's own llms.txt documentation index; it does not say its crawlers read other sites' llms.txt files.
claims.reason: Only mention: "For the complete documentation index, see llms.txt" (its own). No statement that its crawlers read other sites' llms.txt.

claims.claim: Anthropic publishes its own llms.txt for its developer docs, titled "Anthropic Developer Documentation", at platform.claude.com/llms.txt.
claims.reason: File loads at platform.claude.com/llms.txt with H1 "# Anthropic Developer Documentation" and an overview of the API docs.

claims.claim: Anthropic's crawler page (April 7, 2026) lists ClaudeBot, Claude-User and Claude-SearchBot, says they honor robots.txt, and publishes IPs at claude.com/crawling/bots.json.
claims.sourceName: Claude Help Center: Does Anthropic crawl data from the web
claims.reason: Updated Apr 7, 2026; lists all three bots; "Anthropic's Bots respect 'do not crawl' signals by honoring ... robots.txt"; IPs at claude.com/crawling/bots.json.

claims.claim: Perplexity says PerplexityBot surfaces and links sites in Perplexity search and is not used to train AI foundation models; its IPs are at perplexity.com/perplexitybot.json.
claims.reason: "surface and link websites in search results on Perplexity. It is not used to crawl content for AI foundation models." IPs: perplexity.com/perplexitybot.json.

claims.claim: Google verifies its crawlers by reverse DNS (googlebot.com, google.com, googleusercontent.com) or by matching IPs to published JSON lists such as common-crawlers.json.
claims.sourceName: Google Search Central: Verifying Googlebot and other Google crawlers
claims.reason: Reverse DNS: domain "either googlebot.com, google.com, or googleusercontent.com"; or match IPs to JSON lists incl. common-crawlers.json.

claims.claim: Google says GoogleOther is a generic crawler used by product teams, and Google-Extended is a robots.txt token for Gemini training and grounding, not a separate crawler.
claims.sourceName: Google Search Central: Google's common crawlers
claims.reason: GoogleOther "is the generic crawler ... used by various product teams"; Google-Extended is a product token for Gemini training/grounding, no separate UA.

claims.claim: Microsoft publishes Bingbot's IP prefixes as a JSON file at bing.com/toolbox/bingbot.json.
claims.reason: URL serves a JSON file of IPv4 prefixes (e.g. 157.55.39.0/24), creationTime 2024-01-03. Bingbot identity is from the filename only.

claims.claim: Apple says Applebot can be verified by reverse DNS in the applebot.apple.com domain or by matching its IP to CIDRs in applebot.json.
claims.reason: Identified "using reverse DNS in the *.applebot.apple.com domain" or by matching IP to "a CIDR prefix contained in" applebot.json.

claims.claim: Common Crawl says CCBot runs on dedicated IP ranges with reverse DNS, and publishes the ranges at index.commoncrawl.org/ccbot.json.
claims.reason: "CCBot is now run on dedicated IP address ranges with reverse DNS (except over IPv6...)"; ranges "provided as JSON at index.commoncrawl.org/ccbot.json."

claims.claim: Amazon says Amazonbot improves its products and services and may be used to train Amazon AI models; it publishes Amazonbot IP addresses at developer.amazon.com/amazonbot/ip-addresses/.
claims.reason: "Amazonbot is used to improve our products and services ... and may be used to train Amazon AI models." IPs at developer.amazon.com/amazonbot/ip-addresses/.

claims.claim: Semrush (September 28, 2026) reports that from mid-August to late October 2025, Search Engine Land's llms.txt got zero visits from Google-Extended, GPTBot, PerplexityBot or ClaudeBot.
claims.reason: Sept 28, 2026: "From mid-August to late October 2025, the llms.txt page received zero visits from Google-Extended ..., GPTBot ..., PerplexityBot, or ClaudeBot."

claims.claim: Ahrefs studied 137,210 domains with traffic in May 2026: 28% publish llms.txt, and 97% of the ~38,000 valid files got no requests in May. SEO audit tools were the top requester.
claims.reason: 137,210 domains with May 2026 traffic; 28% publish; "Of the ~38,000 domains with a valid file, 97% saw no requests"; SEO audit tools top at 21.7%.
